base_files.intent.md:
# Accepted intent ONB-1
Owner: Mira, pilot product owner. Decision: whether to expand the onboarding change in August after a July pilot. ONB-1 was accepted on 2026-05-20 before either measurement window.

Primary customer outcome: eligible accounts completing their setup within 24 hours. Target: at least 70% in the observed window. Preserve the overall primary outcome; segment results are explanatory and guardrail evidence.
Guardrails accepted in ONB-1: neither segment's within-24-hour completion rate may fall by more than 5 percentage points versus baseline; total operating cost per eligible account must be at most USD 4. All measures cover the same eligible accounts and windows. Cost includes support labor and onboarding infrastructure; no revenue or retained-value data exists.

Baseline: 2026-06-01 through 2026-06-30 UTC. Observed: 2026-07-01 through 2026-07-30 UTC. Evaluation cutoff: 2026-08-05T00:00:00Z. Accepted maturity policy: all included accounts must have a complete 24-hour observation and each segment must include at least 20 accounts per window. Exports satisfy this policy; there are no missing observations. Definitions, eligibility and segment classification are unchanged across windows.

Release record REL-1: the changed onboarding flow was enabled for every eligible July pilot account at first setup on 2026-07-01. June accounts used the previous flow. Exposure is verified in the aggregate register. This was an observational pilot, not randomized. The assisted segment had a staffing vacancy throughout July; support policy otherwise remained unchanged. The product owner has not accepted different targets.

# Supplied notes

## N1 — Harbor operator, episode H-7
2026-08-12 interview notes. Before any mockup, the operator described their last missing-receipt task: they used the product's existing search and found it in about three minutes. They did not report a failed lookup or a cost consequence. After the interviewer showed the proposed receipt-assistant mockup and asked 'Would saving hours with this be helpful?', the operator said 'That looks useful.' No purchase or trial commitment was requested.

## N2 — Harbor buyer, same episode H-7
2026-08-12 interview notes from a separate conversation about the same invoice. The buyer said the delay was an internal approval, not locating the receipt: 'We would not pay extra for receipt search.'

## N3 — Cedar operator, episode C-2
2026-08-14 interview notes. The operator used the current export for month-end and said it met the need. Asked 'Would saving hours be helpful?', they answered yes. They had not seen or used the proposed assistant.

## N4 — Sponsor summary
Derived from N1, N2 and N3, with no additional customer contact. 'Three interviews prove demand for the assistant. Both Harbor interviews independently validate the missing-receipt problem.' The sponsor prefers launching the assistant this quarter.

base_files.README.md:
# Exception-desk research exercise
All records are synthetic. The approved source set comprises the study brief, original text notes, aggregate account counts and finance assumptions. No recordings, contacts, live accounts or recruitment permissions exist.
base_files.study-brief.md:
# Study brief ST-1
Decision owner: Arun, operations product lead. Our current invoice product already supports named exception owners and weekly reminders. There is no managed desk today. Sponsor hypothesis: accounts with at least 20 invoice exceptions per month may value a service that ensures each exception has an owner and follows up. A software feature, adopting existing owner rules, a service, or no change are possible directions.

The account export covers all 40 active accounts in July 2026. Accounts are disjoint, the exception-count definition is stable, and the information-sharing flag is a contractual capability, not consent to this proposed service or to research. The service would require the account to be allowed to share exception summaries. There is no evidence yet of how many eligible accounts would buy.

Three accounts were purposively chosen for interviews: Bay and Elm have at least 20 exceptions per month; Pine has fewer. Bay's operator and buyer discuss the same episode B-4. None of the interviewees used the proposed managed desk. The original supplied notes, rather than recordings or transcripts, are the inspected medium.
base_files.notes.md:
# Original study notes

## B1 — Bay operator, episode B-4, pre-concept
The last month-end handoff had 26 exceptions. Ownership was maintained in a chat thread because the operator did not know named owners were already available in the product. They spent about two hours reconciling the thread and spreadsheet that week. They want an accountable next person, not more reminders to everyone. This is one reported episode, not a measured monthly savings series.

## B2 — Bay buyer, episode B-4, pre-concept
The buyer said an approval-policy dispute caused part of that same delay. They can authorize sharing exception summaries under the current contract, but have not agreed to buy a new service. After the interviewer described a USD 90/month managed desk, they said 'Perhaps, if it actually gets the right owner involved.' No trial, budget approval or purchase was agreed.

## E1 — Elm operator, episode E-3, pre-concept
The account has 23 exceptions in a typical month. A previous service repeatedly chased the wrong owner. They now hold a short internal triage meeting, which they consider sufficient. The account's contract does not permit sharing exception summaries externally. They declined a general request to hear about the new service. No reason beyond current process sufficiency and sharing constraints was recorded.

## P1 — Pine operator, episode P-8, pre-concept
With seven exceptions that month, the operator used the existing named-owner rules successfully. They reported no unresolved ownership delay and did not want a managed desk. No concept was shown.

## S1 — Sponsor interpretation
Derived from B1, B2, E1 and P1, not a new source family. 'The two Bay interviews independently show strong willingness to pay. We can sell to all 12 high-exception accounts and save each two hours every week.'
base_files.finance.md:
# Proposed-service assumptions FC-1
All amounts are USD per month. Proposed price: 90 per participating account. Variable delivery cost: 30 per participating account. Incremental fixed program cost: 300 per month, incurred if the service operates, not a sunk existing cost. Qualified service capacity: at most eight participating accounts per month. No other revenue, cost, adoption or customer-hour valuation inputs are supplied. These are planning assumptions, not observed economics or accepted pricing.

base_files.context.md:
# Goal and source evidence G-1
Goal: let the internal pilot team import a file safely and explain what happened to an auditor afterward. In the last observed pilot session, three of ten files had a header-mapping error, two had duplicate rows, and one had both. These are ten observed files, not a population forecast. Existing behavior imports immediately, does not detect duplicates and produces no persisted record of an import. Operators currently compare spreadsheets manually.

R1 proposes a mapping preview before import; it does not itself detect duplicate rows. R2 proposes duplicate detection using the accepted mapping. R3 proposes a record of the import decision and result, not a general cross-workspace activity browser. R4 is unrelated cross-workspace federation and remains deferred. R5 was considered and rejected; its current note still records its intended internal-only meaning. No current human-selected set is established in these source files.

For the scoped internal pilot, the supplied engineering and QA estimates include the needed developer checks, documentation and acceptance checks. No other required work is asserted. Estimates and dates remain pre-PRD planning assumptions.

base_files.calendar.md:
# CAL-1 and estimates E-1
Week 1 begins Monday 2026-09-07. One qualified engineer is available one full day each Monday through Friday, with no other assigned work. One qualified QA reviewer is available one full day each Thursday and Friday. No work occurs outside those days; no overtime or additional people are available. A role can work on at most one item per day. Engineering and QA may work in parallel on different items. Effort can be split across a role's available days.

An item's QA starts only on a day after all of its engineering is complete. R2 engineering starts only on a day after R1 QA is complete. R1 and R3 have no upstream dependencies. The pilot is ready only after QA is complete for every selected item. R4 and R5 have no supplied estimates and are not prerequisites for R1, R2 or R3.
